summary: Hyperammonemic encephalopathy (HE) is a severe complication of sepsis-induced liver injury (SILI), often associated with sepsis. title: Brain Structure and Differential Response to Family-Centered Prevention: Evidence for Anterior Cingulate Cortex Moderation in a Randomized Controlled Trial.
summary: Family-centered prevention programs improve youth self-regulation, yet intervention effects are heterogeneous, and the mechanisms underlying differential response remain poorly understood. Identifying neural metrics that shape responsiveness to prevention may advance theory and inform program refinement. This study examined whether baseline brain structure moderated response to a telehealth adaptation of the Strong African American Families program (T-SAAF), a prevention intervention targeting self-regulation among Black preadolescents. Youth ages 11-12 and their caregivers (N = 170 families) were recruited in North Georgia and randomly assigned to T-SAAF or a no-treatment control condition.

title: Anatomical and radiological analysis of ventricular catheter trajectories: neuronavigation-guided dissection and tractography-based 3D visualization.
summary: Ventricular catheter placement (VCP) is a life-saving intervention frequently performed in emergency departments and intensive care units. The free hand technique is the most commonly used approach for placing catheters. This study demonstrates the anatomical and radiological relationship between catheters inserted through the most commonly used access points and the anatomical structures in their path. Moreover, we calculate the insertion angles and catheter lengths that should be specified during VCP. title: THINKERS-X: multisequence MRI radiomics in a mixture-of-experts model for outcome prediction and exploratory dose-scenario evaluation in lung cancer brain metastases treated with radiosurgery.
summary: We developed THINKERS-X: Lung, the eXtended multimodal evolution of THINKERS-Lung, to determine whether multisequence MRI radiomics provides incremental value for lesion-specific outcome prediction and exploratory dose-scenario evaluation after Gamma Knife radiosurgery (GKRS) for lung cancer brain metastases. We performed a retrospective single-center study of 767 patients with 3,728 lung cancer brain metastases treated with GKRS. THINKERS-X preserved the original mixture-of-experts and discrete-time survival architecture while adding a dedicated computational neuroradiology expert. title: Facial emotion recognition of sadness relates to superior parietal gray matter volume in mild cognitive impairment.
summary: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) is associated with early, regionally selective neurodegenerative changes that may affect socioemotional functioning before atrophy becomes widespread. This study examined whether structural brain alterations in MCI relate to facial emotion recognition performance. Sixty adults (30 MCI, 30 healthy controls), aged 50-86 years, completed neuropsychological testing, the Facial emotion composite Task, and structural MRI. Whole-brain voxel-based morphometry revealed no significant gray matter volume differences between groups. title: Slow-wave sleep selectively amplifies network signatures of the presumed epileptogenic zone in focal epilepsy.
summary: Slow-wave sleep increases interictal epileptiform discharges (IEDs) and seizures in focal epilepsy, but how sleep stages reshape epileptogenic tissue remains unclear. We assessed whether sleep stages selectively modulate network properties of the presumed epileptogenic zone (pEZ) relative to irritative (IZ) and non-involved (NIZ) zones. We studied 22 patients with drug-resistant focal epilepsy undergoing pre-surgical intracranial electroencephalography (iEEG). IED-free resting-state epochs spanned four vigilance stages: wakefulness, non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep stages 2 and 3, and rapid eye movement (REM) sleep. title: A Standardized Workflow for Multimodal Assessment of Right-to-Left Shunt-Related Ischemic Brain Injury.
summary: Right-to-left shunt (RLS) has been associated with cryptogenic stroke, migraine, and other neurological conditions in which ischemic brain injury may be clinically relevant. In routine practice, however, assessment is often fragmented. Shunt presence may be documented, but shunt burden, provoked versus non-provoked patterns, anatomical complexity, and MRI-defined brain injury are not always integrated into a reproducible workflow. Here, we describe a standardized protocol for multimodal assessment of RLS-related ischemic brain injury in a clinically selected cohort. title: Clinicoradiological Findings of COVID-19-Associated Mucormycosis in a Referral Tertiary Care.
summary: Mucormycosis, an opportunistic fungal infection, has surged during the COVID-19 pandemic, especially with the delta variant, due to factors like steroid use and diabetes. This study examines radiological features through computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings in COVID-19-associated mucormycosis (CAM) patients. This single-center cross-sectional study conducted between March 2021 and March 2022 at a tertiary care center involved COVID-19 patients over 18 diagnosed with mucormycosis through pathological and endoscopic findings. title: Significance of Carotid Intima-media Thickness and Bone Mineral Density in Cerebrovascular Disease in Health Screening Examinees.
summary: Carotid intima-media thickness (CIMT) and bone mineral density (BMD) are key markers of vascular and skeletal health, respectively. While each has been linked to cerebrovascular disease individually, their combined effect remains unclear. This study assessed the independent and interactive roles of CIMT and BMD in cerebrovascular disease among asymptomatic adults undergoing health screening. We retrospectively analyzed data of 1447 participants who underwent CIMT measurement, BMD testing, and brain magnetic resonance (MR) imaging with MR angiography at a general hospital between January 2020 and March 2022. title: Not All Transverse Sinus Stenoses Behave the Same: Distinct Flow Phenotypes on Phase-Contrast MRI.
summary: Background Transverse sinus stenosis is usually assessed by its anatomical appearance, although stenoses with similar morphology may not have the same local flow behavior. This study evaluated peak velocity changes across transverse sinus stenoses using phase-contrast magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and explored whether distinct hemodynamic patterns could be identified. title: The Mask of Delirium: Uncovering a Presumed Cardioembolic Stroke Through Comprehensive Clinical Evaluation.
summary: Delirium and aphasia exhibit overlapping clinical features, complicating the diagnosis of acute neurological disturbances in older adults. Both conditions impair communication and orientation, leading to incoherence; however, they arise from distinct pathophysiological mechanisms and require different management strategies. This case concerns an 83-year-old woman with a 48-hour history of acute-onset confusion and abnormal speech. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed an acute infarct in the inferior division of the left middle cerebral artery (MCA) territory, with cardioembolism considered the likely cause. title: Diagnostic challenges of masked arginine vasopressin deficiency in neurosarcoidosis complicated by sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor use.
summary: A wide variety of endocrine disorders caused by sarcoidosis have been reported to date. We report the case of an 82-year-old male patient who presented with hypercalcemia and anterior pituitary hormone deficiency at the time of his sarcoidosis diagnosis and was subsequently diagnosed with arginine vasopressin deficiency (AVP-D) 6 months after the initiation of glucocorticoid therapy. title: Correlation of blood biomarkers with microstructural brain injury in survivors of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest.
summary: In-hospital mortality among resuscitated out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) patients remains high. Identifying patients who will benefit from intensive care while avoiding prolonged, potentially unnecessary treatments is essential. Blood-based biomarkers provide a novel method for evaluating brain injury. title: Deep white-matter tracts link docosahexaenoic acid status to cognitive performance in human adolescents.
summary: Docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) is a polyunsaturated fatty acid enriched in neuronal membranes and myelin, linked to cognitive performance. Yet, nutritional interventions show inconsistent cognitive benefits due to a limited understanding of the neural pathways connecting DHA status to human cognition. We studied 99 adolescents selected from both extremes of performance on a national scholastic examination. Participants completed assessments of intellectual ability, provided erythrocyte DHA samples, and underwent multimodal MRI. title: Malignant cerebral edema secondary to herpes simplex virus encephalitis requiring decompressive hemicraniectomy.
summary: Herpes simplex encephalitis (HSE) is a severe viral infection of the central nervous system that most commonly affects the temporal lobes and limbic structures. Although most cases are managed medically with intravenous acyclovir, rare cases can rapidly progress to malignant cerebral edema, mass effect, and neurologic deterioration requiring surgical intervention. We report the case of a 57-year-old woman presenting with altered mental status, headache, vomiting, myalgias, and focal neurologic deficits. title: Short-term responses across two sequential plant-based activity sessions: an exploratory fixed-order pilot study.
summary: Structured plant-based activities combine natural materials, purposeful manual work, sensory engagement, and social interaction, but direct comparisons of practical formats in community adults remain limited. We characterized short-term responses during two sequential sessions and compared within-session changes. Twenty-five adults participated in a single-group, fixed-order pilot study. Session 1 involved horticultural crafting; 1 week later, Session 2 involved balm crafting followed by horticultural crafting. Twenty-three attended both sessions. title: Comparative Dosimetric Evaluation of Tomotherapy with a 1-cm Field Width versus Volumetric-modulated Arc Therapy for Whole-brain Radiotherapy with Hippocampal Avoidance.
summary: Hippocampal-avoidance whole-brain radiotherapy (HA-WBRT) reduces radiation dose to the hippocampal neural stem-cell niche, helping preserve neurocognitive function in patients with brain metastases. The objective of this study is to compare tomotherapy using a 1-cm field width with four-arc volumetric-modulated arc therapy (VMAT) for HA-WBRT. title: Electroencephalography Changes in Emotional Recognition: A Signal Processing Approach Using Wavelet Features.
summary: motion recognition using electroencephalography (EEG) has gained significant attention in the fields of affective computing and human-computer interaction due to its ability to capture real-time neural responses. EEG signal variations associated with emotional states can be analysed using wavelet-based signal processing within the arousal-valence framework. This study aims to analyse EEG signal variations associated with emotional states using a wavelet-based signal processing approach within the arousal-valence framework. title: An explainable machine learning model based on multidimensional task-state electroencephalography for identifying attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder comorbid developmental dyslexia.
summary: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and developmental dyslexia (DD) are highly comorbid, yet objective differentiation from individual disorders remains challenging due to the lack of neurophysiological biomarkers. This study aimed to develop an interpretable machine learning model leveraging multidimensional task-state EEG features to distinguish ADHD-DD comorbidity from ADHD and typical development (TD). Ninety children (27 ADHD-DD, 40 ADHD, 23 TD) underwent EEG during a VSWM task. title: A sliding window and Fourier decomposition method based 1D-CNN framework for motor imagery EEG classification.
summary: Electroencephalography (EEG) signal classification is fundamental requirement for effective motor imagery (MI) brain-computer interface (BCI) applications. However, current MI classification methods often depend on handcrafted spatial filtering or complex time-frequency transformations that increase computational complexity. To mitigate this limitation, we propose a unified architecture that integrates a sliding window (SW), a Fourier decomposition method (FDM), and a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) for MI-EEG classification. title: Tensor decomposition reveals discrete cortical reorganization under graded propofol anesthesia.
summary: Although propofol-induced anesthesia is known to suppress consciousness by promoting low-frequency frontal oscillations through thalamocortical circuits, a comprehensive understanding of its whole-brain coupling feature set remains elusive. Specifically, the global reorganization of nonlinear cross-frequency coupling remains poorly characterized due to analytical limitations. We analyzed 64-channel EEG data from 17 participants across five states (awake and target propofol concentrations of 1, 2, 3, and 4 mcg/ml, defined as States 1 to 5). title: Basal Forebrain Volume is Associated With Cortical Amyloid Burden in Cognitively Unimpaired Older Adults at Varying Genetic Risk for Alzheimer's Disease.
source: PubMed · Am J Geriatr Psychiatry Open Sci Educ Pract
summary: In mild cognitive impairment and dementia due to Alzheimer's disease (AD), postmortem and in vivo neuroimaging studies have demonstrated significant neuronal loss in the basal forebrain cholinergic system (BFCS), which provides the primary cholinergic input to the cerebral cortex. title: Copenhagen Magnetic Personalized Accelerated Brain Circuit Therapy (CoMPACT) trial: study protocol for a randomized, double-blinded, sham-controlled, three-armed, parallel-group trial of transcranial magnetic stimulation for treatment-resistant depression.
summary: Treatment-resistant depression (TRD), characterized by poor response to conventional antidepressant therapies, remains a major clinical challenge. Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) of the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC) has emerged as a promising alternative. Employing intermittent theta burst stimulation (iTBS), TMS protocols have yielded rapid antidepressant effects in recent accelerated treatment studies. These findings warrant further investigation in larger samples to confirm efficacy and in-depth investigation into the underlying mechanisms. title: Peritoneal neuroendocrine carcinoma of unknown primary with markedly elevated alpha-fetoprotein: a case report.
summary: Peritoneal neuroendocrine carcinoma(NEC) is primarily metastatic, with primary cases being exceedingly rare. The relationship between alpha-fetoprotein(AFP) and neuroendocrine carcinoma remains unclear. In this report, we present a patient with peritoneal neuroendocrine carcinoma who exhibited significantly elevated AFP levels. Extensive evaluation revealed no obvious primary site outside the peritoneum; however, occult gastrointestinal origin could not be entirely excluded. title: Case Report: Melanocyte-associated mTORC1-related molecular features in an atypical large congenital melanocytic naevus.
summary: Congenital melanocytic naevi (CMN) are usually associated with activating alterations in NRAS or BRAF, but some extensive lesions lack detectable canonical hotspot variants. We report a 9-year-old boy with a large craniofacial CMN involving the face, scalp, upper eyelid and bulbar conjunctiva, with deep extension, mechanical ptosis and secondary amblyopia. summary: Aim: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are emerging as important mediators in myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs), but the characteristics of distinct EV subtypes remain unclear. This study aimed to characterize the molecular heterogeneity of MEG-01-derived large EVs (lEVs) and small EVs (sEVs). title: Validating the standard model of diffusion MRI in white matter with numerical substrates.
summary: The non-invasive estimation of intra- and extracellular microstructural parameters using biophysical models has been a major focus in brain microstructure imaging with MRI. The Standard Model (SM) of diffusion in white matter (WM) provides a unifying framework for various modelling approaches, representing axons as impermeable sticks embedded within a locally anisotropic extra-axonal space. title: Multiscale neural signatures of long-lag repetition learning: a simultaneous fNIRS-EEG study.
summary: Repetition-based learning supports word recognition and reading fluency, yet its neural mechanisms remain poorly understood, particularly where deficits in consolidating repeated linguistic input may underlie reading and language difficulties. Establishing reliable neural markers of repetition-based learning is a critical first step toward characterizing the phenotypes of these difficulties in children. summary: Reading and speech recognition rely on multi-level processing that builds from basic visual or sound features to complete word representations, yet details of these processing hierarchies (in particular those for spoken words) are still poorly understood. title: Fibrolipomatous Hamartoma of the Median Nerve Misdiagnosed as a Palmar Space Abscess: A Case Report.
source: PubMed · Int Med Case Rep J
summary: Fibrolipomatous hamartoma (FLH), also categorized under lipomatosis of nerve, is a rare, is an uncommon benign fibrofatty lesion of the peripheral nerves that most commonly affects the median nerve. summary: Congenital Chagas disease remains an underdiagnosed cause of neonatal morbidity and mortality in endemic regions. Although most infected neonates are asymptomatic or present with nonspecific findings, severe and atypical manifestations involving the central nervous system or coexistence with genetic disorders are rarely reported. The full spectrum of neurologic injury and potential interactions between Trypanosoma cruzi infection and fetal developmental conditions remain poorly characterized. summary: Fluid and crystallized intelligence have recently been hypothesized to reflect the brain network's capacity to facilitate transitions into hard-to-reach, high-energy states, measured via modal controllability, and easy-to-reach, low-energy states, measured via average controllability, respectively. title: Case Report: Seronegative rhombencephalitis presenting with ocular flutter and ataxia as a potential sentinel manifestation of gastric adenocarcinoma.
summary: This case report aims to highlight the rare clinical phenotype of seronegative autoimmune rhombencephalitis presenting with ocular flutter and ataxia, and to emphasize its potential association with underlying paraneoplastic neurological syndromes. title: Anatomical determinants of DTI-ALPS: Effects of ROI definition, ventricular morphology, and periventricular deformation.
summary: The diffusion tensor image analysis along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS) index is increasingly used as a non-invasive MRI biomarker proposed to reflect glymphatic and perivascular function, yet the anatomical validity and measurement stability of the metric remain incompletely characterised. title: Neurovascular uncoupling in type 2 diabetes mellitus: multimodal MRI reveals the association between hippocampal and subcortical structures dysfunction and cognitive decline.
summary: To investigate the efficiency of neurovascular coupling (NVC) in hippocampal and subcortical structures in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and its relations with cognition and glycemic control, and to characterize multimodal MRI features of T2DM-related cognitive decline. title: Age-related spinal degenerative diseases: a quantitative analysis of the dynamic evolution, knowledge structure, and research frontiers in neurological damage.
summary: Aging is the primary risk factor for the four major spinal degenerative diseases of lumbar disc herniation (LDH), cervical spondylosis (CS), lumbar spinal stenosis (LSS) and thoracic disc herniation (TDH). These diseases can lead to severe neurological dysfunction, chronic neuropathic pain and a decline in the quality of life in elderly patients. title: Clinical correlation of hemodynamic parameters using blood flow prediction model in cerebrovascular arteries.
summary: Patient-specific hemodynamic assessment is pivotal for optimizing treatment strategies in cerebrovascular interventions; however, conventional modalities are often limited by restricted clinical accessibility or prolonged acquisition times. summary: Adamantinomatous craniopharyngioma is an uncommon benign epithelial tumor arising from remnants of Rathke's pouch within the sellar-suprasellar region. summary: Photon measurement density function (PMDF) determines the measurement locations and their associated sensitivity to the hemodynamic changes for an fNIRS channel. summary: Intravenous lidocaine is used as an adjuvant to total intravenous anesthesia (TIVA). Conventional MRI provides detailed anatomical information but has a limited capacity to evaluate tumor biology. Intravoxel Incoherent Motion (IVIM) is an advanced functional MRI technique that simultaneously measures tissue cellularity and microvascular perfusion without contrast agents, providing deeper insights into the tumor microenvironment. summary: Male breast cancer (MBC) is rare, accounting for approximately 1% of all breast cancers. title: Pharmacologically altered androgens, brain activation and response inhibition in a stop-signal task in male heavy drinkers.
summary: Heavy episodic drinking (HED) is highly prevalent in men and a major risk factor for Alcohol Use Disorder (AUD). title: Case Report: McLeod syndrome caused by a nonsense variant c.484C > T (p.Gln162Ter) in the XK gene in a Chinese Han family.
summary: McLeod syndrome (MLS) is a rare X-linked neuroacanthocytosis caused by pathogenic variants in XK, and is characterized by hyperkinetic movements, peripheral neuropathy and myopathy with hyperCKemia, acanthocytosis and cardiomyopathy. title: Decoding morality through EEG with ML: rigour, risks, and the road ahead.
summary: The quest to decode morality through electroencephalography (EEG) with machine learning (ML) is as much about confronting the risks of opaque algorithms as it is about harnessing their scientific promise. title: Clinical features and outcomes of atezolizumab-associated encephalitis.
summary: To explore the clinical characteristics of atezolizumab-associated encephalitis and to provide clinical evidence for diagnosis and treatment. title: Artificial intelligence-assisted categorization of interictal abnormalities in adult long-term electroencephalographic monitoring: Comparable diagnostic accuracy with marked efficiency gain.
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) classifies routine electroencephalograms (EEGs) with expert-level accuracy, but interpretation of long-term EEG monitoring (LTM) remains reliant on time-intensive visual review.
